title: The Power of the Next-Action Decision
coreMove: Turn each vague commitment into the next visible physical action so engagement becomes possible.
sourcePressure: This principles chapter explains why deciding the concrete next action reduces stuckness and changes how people engage with commitments.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating next action as a motivational slogan rather than a concrete decision about the body’s next move.
sourceAnchorNote: The source sidecar contains no chapter-specific named people, named studies, or named places. Use only the listed GTD terms, official metadata, or supported artifacts; do not invent anecdotes.

sourceAnchors.name: next-action decision
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies this as the principle-level power in Chapter 12.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The next-action decision is the moment a concern stops being fog and starts asking for a hand, a phone, a document, or a door.

sourceAnchors.name: concrete move
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar ties concreteness and reduced stuckness to the next-action decision.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Concrete means you can see the verb happen from across the room.

hook: stress is not about having too much to do
a messy desk proves the system is broken
counterintuition: the real problem is not time but attention
this is not about doing more but doing what matters
the simple move is actually the powerful one
tryThisNow: set a timer and write everything down
pick one task and make it specific
review your list and choose a priority
examples: timestamp plus name plus laptop plus decision repeated across all six examples
home kitchen clutter as mental-load shorthand

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: a four-person architecture firm during facade revision standup

exampleSpecs.domain: a homeowner reviving a stalled kitchen renovation without generic home clutter

exampleSpecs.stakes: the house could enter winter with exposed subfloor because research never became action

exampleSpecs.firstImage: two printed project lists side by side

exampleSpecs.domain: a mobile app team retrospective after missing a press window
exampleSpecs.audience: a product lead guiding engineers and designer through a late launch
exampleSpecs.stakes: a competitor already claimed the release narrative

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: translate vague tasks into physical next actions
evaluate whether an action is concrete enough

tryThisNowSpec: Rewrite one vague list item as a physical verb plus object, such as call, email, open, print, ask, or place.
